title: Open restriction preserves the comparison augmentation and its normalization
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $T$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $
u_S^*\dashv
u_{S,*}$ for $S=T,V$ be the comparison adjunctions with ordinary units $\eta^0$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and use inverse-image restrictions $j_e^{-1},j_p^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Write $ eta_F:
u_V^*j_e^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}j_p^{-1}
u_T^*F$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Identify $j_e^{-1}
u_{T,*}G=
u_{V,*}j_p^{-1}G$ by the identity of sections $G(W	o V	o T)$ on every etale $W	o V$, as in [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit].

Let $F$ be an etale $A$-module sheaf and $h:
u_T^*F	o J$ any bounded-below injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Set $I=
u_{T,*}J$, $a=
u_{T,*}(h)\eta^0_F$, $F_V=j_e^{-1}F$, $J_V=j_p^{-1}J$ and
$$h_V=(j_p^{-1}h) eta_F,\qquad a_V=
u_{V,*}(h_V)\eta^0_{F_V}.$$
Then $h_V:
u_V^*F_V	o J_V$ is a bounded-below injective resolution, $
u_{V,*}J_V=j_e^{-1}I$, and $a_V$ is an etale bounded-below injective resolution representing the derived unit under its canonical injective computation [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective, lem-pur-support-comparison-common-injectives]. In these identifications the ordinary unit and the augmentations satisfy the actual equalities
$$j_e^{-1}(\eta^0_F)=
u_{V,*}( eta_F)\eta^0_{F_V},$$
$$a_V=
u_{V,*}(j_p^{-1}h)
u_{V,*}( eta_F)\eta^0_{F_V}=j_e^{-1}(a).$$
For each etale $W	o V$, evaluation of $j_e^{-1}I$ and $J_V$ gives the same complex $J(W	o T)$, with its actual differential and all restriction maps.

These are identifications of augmented resolutions, natural in chain maps: for a second pair $F',h':
u_T^*F'	o J'$ and $f:F	o F'$, $t:J	o J'$ with $th=h'
u_T^*f$, put $f_V=j_e^{-1}f$, $t_V=j_p^{-1}t$. Then
$$t_Vh_V=h'_V
u_V^*(f_V),\qquad
u_{V,*}(t_V)a_V=a'_V f_V.$$
The canonical injective computation isomorphisms for the restricted resolutions commute with these maps. No assertion about supported or global comparison morphisms, or connecting morphisms, is included.

source.place: Tag 03CF (lemma-localize-morphism), localization square and its direct-image/restriction identity; with proetale.tex Tags 099V (lemma-relative-comparison) and 09B1 (lemma-compare-derived). Agent-formulated augmentation normalization extracted from returned section-model steps 2 and 4, the restriction identity in step 1, and open naturality in step 6; uses the exact canonical unit normalization of lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit.

proof.text: An open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence weakly etale. Use the adopted source instance ProEtale.preservesInjectiveObjects_localizationRestriction directly, specialized to ModuleCat A and j, to show every term of the restricted complex is injective. Restriction is the continuous sheaf pushforward, so it preserves finite limits; the existing openImmersionRestrictionLowerStarAdjunction also makes it a left adjoint, so it preserves finite colimits. The exact-functor homology instances of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] therefore preserve the quasi-isomorphism h. Precompose with the canonical comparison beta and the degree-zero source transport from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback, lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit]. An additive functor preserves the lower bound, already recorded by mapCochainComplexPlus. Thus this very h_V is the required bounded-below injective resolution; the slice-equivalence and unbounded derived-evaluation parts of the larger restriction theorem are unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 03CF (lemma-localize-morphism), localization square; proetale.tex Tag 099V; homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), termwise application

proof.text:
Use the restriction identifications and the actual unit equation of [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit]. Its map $a_F$ is $ eta_F^{-1}$, and its direct-image map $c$ is the identity on sections in the identifications of the present statement. It says $
u_{V,*}( eta_F^{-1})j_e^{-1}(\eta^0_F)=\eta^0_{F_V}$. Compose on the left with $
u_{V,*}( eta_F)$ and cancel the inverse factors. This gives the required equality $j_e^{-1}(\eta^0_F)=
u_{V,*}( eta_F)\eta^0_{F_V}$, with exactly the prescribed canonical $ eta$, rather than a newly chosen pullback isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03CF (lemma-localize-morphism), sectionwise restriction/direct-image identity; canonical-unit normalization in lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit

proof.text:
The direct-image/restriction identification $c_G$ of [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit] is the identity on $G(W	o V	o T)$. Applied degreewise to $J$, it identifies $
u_{V,*}J_V$ with $j_e^{-1}
u_{T,*}J=j_e^{-1}I$, and, applied to $h$, identifies $
u_{V,*}(j_p^{-1}h)$ with $j_e^{-1}(
u_{T,*}h)$. Expand the definition of $h_V$ and use functoriality and step 2:
$$a_V=
u_{V,*}(j_p^{-1}h)
u_{V,*}( eta_F)\eta^0_{F_V}=j_e^{-1}(
u_{T,*}h)j_e^{-1}(\eta^0_F)=j_e^{-1}a.$$
Every equality is in the category of augmented complexes under the stated restriction identifications.

source.place: Tag 03CF (lemma-localize-morphism), final assertion and displayed evaluation calculation in its proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-support-comparison-common-injectives] with the scheme $V$, the same finite commutative ring $A$, and the resolution $h_V$ established in step 1. It gives that $a_V:F_V\to\nu_{V,*}J_V$ is an etale bounded-below injective resolution and that, under its canonical injective computation isomorphism, $Qa_V$ is the derived unit. No constructibility assumption on $F_V$ is needed. The sectionwise identity from [lem-pur-comparison-pullback-open-unit] evaluates, on every etale $W\to V$, to $J^n(W\to T)$ in each degree $n$. It evaluates the differential to $d_J^n(W\to T)$, and an arrow $W'\to W$ to the restriction map of $J^n$ along that same arrow over $T$. Thus these are the same complexes, differentials and restriction maps, not just isomorphic cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), clause (2); Tag 09B1 (lemma-compare-derived), clause (2); sites.tex Tag 03CF, sectionwise evaluation

proof.text:
Naturality of $ eta$ in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives $(j_p^{-1}
u_T^*f) eta_F= eta_{F'}
u_V^*f_V$. Restrict the given equation $th=h'
u_T^*f$ and substitute this identity:
$$t_Vh_V=(j_p^{-1}t)(j_p^{-1}h) eta_F=(j_p^{-1}h')(j_p^{-1}
u_T^*f) eta_F=h'_V
u_V^*f_V.$$
The unit of the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is a natural transformation, so $
u_{V,*}(
u_V^*f_V)\eta^0_{F_V}=\eta^0_{F'_V}f_V$. Consequently
$$
u_{V,*}(t_V)a_V=
u_{V,*}(t_Vh_V)\eta^0_{F_V}=
u_{V,*}(h'_V)\eta^0_{F'_V}f_V=a'_Vf_V.$$
This is an equality of chain maps, with no choice of a comparison lift.

source.place: Tag 03CF (lemma-localize-morphism), natural localization square; ordinary adjunction unit naturality

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-support-comparison-common-injectives] to both restricted resolutions to obtain theta and theta-prime with their canonical computation and derived-unit normalization equations. Step 5 gives the augmentation chain-map equality. The first augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by the same common-injectives theorem, so its image under the bounded-below derived localization Q is invertible. Precompose the desired theta/theta-prime naturality square with that image. Functoriality of Q and the augmentation equality turn its left side into Q(f_V) followed by Qa-prime and theta-prime. Replace Qa-prime theta-prime and Qa theta by the two derived units. The remaining equality is precisely naturality of the unit of the derived comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Cancel the invertible image of the first augmentation. Thus the canonical computation isomorphisms commute with every compatible chain map without reconstructing them or making any additional choice.
